subject: Nexara MSA redlines — indemnity step-down & evidence handoff
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nexara.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Thorpe <mike.thorpe@nexara.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Nexara MSA redlines — indemnity section and evidence handoff

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Attached is Nexara's proposed redline to the MSA and Order Form (nexara-msaredline-v1.docx). The legal team is focused on two items we want to close quickly:

1) Indemnity for third-party IP claims — we want stronger express defense/control but accept a step-down on damages (i.e., customer responsibility for direct damages up to a cap, redwood takes defense above that).
2) Evidence & notice — we need a clear owner for collecting technical evidence (logs, sample inputs, runtime snapshots) and an SLA for handoff when a claim arises.

Open questions from our side:
- Who at Redwood will take responsibility for gathering model runtime artifacts?
- Would Redwood accept a 30-day notice and a 45-day evidence staging period after notice?

We can be flexible on carveouts (OSS, third-party data) but need the process spelled out. Attaching draft and looping in Mike from procurement for timeline.

Can we do a short call tomorrow to walk through defense/control options so we can finalize redlines?

Thanks,
Sarah Lin
Legal Counsel, Nexara Robotics
attachments: nexara-msaredline-v1.docx
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nexara.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nexara MSA redlines — indemnity section and evidence handoff

Hi Sarah — thanks for the redline. Quick read-through below and I've attached a short comment set (redline-comments-stephanie.pdf). High-level position and proposed compromise: 

- Defense/control: Redwood agrees to assume defense/control for third-party IP claims that are directly tied to model outputs generated by a Redwood-served model, subject to a monetary cap tied to the relevant Order Form (we recommend $2M for this deal given expected ARR). Below the cap, we propose a step-down where Nexara has primary responsibility for settlement up to the cap (i.e., reverse ladder approach).

- Evidence owner: Redwood can commit to preserving and producing model runtime artifacts (KV cache snapshots, prompt+response bundles, tokenized inputs where available) when the claim arises, provided Nexara gives reasonable access and an agreed list of evidence items. We propose standardizing the list in an "Evidence Bundle Template" and will attach a template (evidence-bundle-template.xlsx) to the order form.

- Notice & staging: 30-day notice + 45-day staging is reasonable. To operationalize: require initial notice, a request for evidence, then a 45-day window for evidence staging from Redwood's side. If additional third-party subpoenas are required, add an exception.

Action items:
1) Lauren/legal to draft a tracked redline with the step-down language and caps.
2) Ben/sales to confirm commercial cap target ($2M) or provide counter.
3) Schedule 30-min call with Nexara legal + procurement to align on evidence list/timing.

Proposed call slots: Tomorrow 11:00-11:30 PT or Thu 10:00-10:30 PT. Which works?

Thanks — I'll draft the tracked redline after Ben confirms cap.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
redwood.com
attachments: redline-comments-stephanie.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nexara MSA redlines — indemnity step-down & evidence handoff

Quick note — I'm supportive of the step-down approach but want to avoid open-ended exposure. A couple of commercial guardrails:

- Limit Redwood's defense commitment to a per-claim cap and an annual aggregate (same as order form cap + 2x aggregate).
- Add an insurance offset clause: if Nexara has applicable insurance that covers all/part of a claim, Redwood's indemnity is reduced accordingly.
- Keep evidence staging SLAs tight to avoid prolonged collects (we should push for maximum 60 days including customer-provided evidence).

Lauren — can you prepare a short paragraph on settlement approval rights and control split? Procurement will need that for the PO.

Ben
Senior Account Exec — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nexara.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Thorpe <mike.thorpe@nexara.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nexara MSA redlines — indemnity step-down & evidence handoff

Thanks, Stephanie and Ben — helpful positions. We reviewed and Nexara can accept a step-down approach if three items are explicit in the redline:

1) A clear timeline: notice (30 days), Redwood evidence staging (45 days), and a 15-day cure/settlement consultation window.
2) A mandatory evidence owner: Redwood to produce the evidence bundle as defined in the Excel template; Nexara will be responsible for providing customer-side logs and any contractual opt-out notices.
3) Settlement rights: both parties must consent to settlements that materially assign liability to the other party; unilateral settlements that prejudice the non-settling party are prohibited.

I've attached an updated tracked version (nexara-msaredline-v2.docx) with the three bullets inserted and minor language clarifications. Can we lock a 30-min call Friday to confirm technical evidence items and the cap figure?

Regards,
Sarah
Legal Counsel, Nexara Robotics
